form.title: Cambridge AS Level Science onboarding test

writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.stem: A 2 kW heater runs for 3 hours. How much energy does it use?
items.markingKey: B. 6 kWh. E = P x t = 2 kW x 3 h

items.stem: A 6 V battery drives a current of 2 A through a resistor. What is its resistance?
items.markingKey: D. 3 Ω. R = V ÷ I

items.stem: Two 4 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the combined resistance?
A transformer that increases voltage is called a
items.markingKey: D. step-up transformer. More turns on the secondary coil

items.stem: A transformer has 100 primary turns and 500 secondary turns. The input is 12 V. What is the output?
items.markingKey: A. 60 V. Vs/Vp = Ns/Np = 5

items.stem: Why is electricity transmitted at very high voltage over long distances?
items.answer: A smaller current flows, so less energy is lost as heat
options: A smaller current flows, so less energy is lost as heat
items.markingKey: B. A smaller current flows, so less energy is lost as heat. Power loss = I²R

items.stem: When light passes from air into glass, it
items.answer: slows down and bends towards the normal
options: speeds up and bends away from the normal
does not change direction at any angle
slows down and bends towards the normal
items.markingKey: D. slows down and bends towards the normal. Glass is optically denser

items.stem: Why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?
items.answer: Light from the straw refracts as it leaves the water
options: Light from the straw refracts as it leaves the water
items.markingKey: C. Light from the straw refracts as it leaves the water. Refraction at the surface

items.stem: Light travels at 3 x 10⁸ m/s in air and 2 x 10⁸ m/s in glass. What is the refractive index of the glass?
items.markingKey: A. 1.5. n = speed in air ÷ speed in glass

items.stem: Which of these is an SI base unit?
items.markingKey: D. kilogram. N, J and W are derived units

items.stem: Which of these is a vector quantity?
items.markingKey: A. velocity. Velocity has a direction

items.stem: What are the base units of force (the newton)?
items.markingKey: C. kg m s⁻². F = ma

items.stem: The gradient of a displacement-time graph gives the
items.markingKey: A. velocity. Change in displacement over time

items.stem: A car travels 120 m north in 10 s then 40 m south in 10 s. What is its average velocity?
items.markingKey: D. 4 m/s north. Displacement 80 m north over 20 s

items.stem: A velocity-time graph is a horizontal line above the time axis. What does it show?
items.markingKey: C. Constant velocity, zero acceleration. Gradient is zero

items.stem: A ball is dropped from rest. Ignoring air resistance, what is its speed after 2 s? (g = 10 m/s²)
items.markingKey: B. 20 m/s. v = u + at

items.stem: A car accelerates from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4 s. How far does it travel?
items.markingKey: C. 80 m. s = ½(u + v)t = ½ x 40 x 4

items.stem: A stone is thrown up at 15 m/s. How high does it rise? (g = 10 m/s²)
items.markingKey: A. 11.25 m. v² = u² - 2gs with v = 0

items.stem: Newton's first law says an object keeps moving at constant velocity unless
items.answer: a resultant force acts on it
options: a resultant force acts on it
items.markingKey: A. a resultant force acts on it. Inertia

items.stem: A 2 kg trolley moving at 3 m/s has momentum of
items.markingKey: A. 6 kg m/s. p = mv

items.stem: A 0.5 kg ball hits a wall at 4 m/s and bounces back at 4 m/s. What is the change in momentum?
items.markingKey: D. 4 kg m/s. Direction reverses: 0.5 x (4 - (-4))

items.stem: How many atoms are in one molecule of H₂SO₄?
Acid + alkali gives
items.markingKey: D. a salt and water. Neutralisation

items.stem: Which salt forms when hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide?
items.markingKey: A. sodium chloride. Chloride from HCl

items.stem: The general formula of the alkanes is
items.markingKey: D. CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Saturated hydrocarbons

items.stem: Which test distinguishes an alkene from an alkane?
items.answer: Bromine water is decolourised by the alkene
options: A glowing splint relights with the alkene
Bromine water is decolourised by the alkene
Limewater turns milky with the alkane
items.markingKey: C. Bromine water is decolourised by the alkene. Addition across C=C

items.stem: Ethene and propene belong to the same homologous series. What do they share?
items.answer: The same functional group and general formula
options: The same functional group and general formula
The same number of carbon atoms
items.markingKey: A. The same functional group and general formula. They differ by CH₂

items.stem: A reaction that releases heat to the surroundings is
items.markingKey: C. exothermic. Temperature rises

items.stem: Which metal can be extracted from its oxide by heating with carbon?
items.markingKey: D. iron. Metals below carbon in the reactivity series

items.stem: Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis rather than with carbon?
items.answer: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
options: Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
items.markingKey: A. Aluminium is more reactive than carbon. Carbon cannot reduce it

items.stem: One mole of any substance contains about
items.markingKey: C. 6.02 x 10²³ particles. Avogadro's constant

items.stem: How many moles are in 36 g of water (H₂O, Mr = 18)?
items.markingKey: A. 2 mol. n = m ÷ M

items.stem: What mass of CO₂ forms when 12 g of carbon burns completely? (C = 12, O = 16)
items.markingKey: D. 44 g. 1 mol C gives 1 mol CO₂

items.stem: How many electrons can an s orbital hold?
items.markingKey: B. 2. Two electrons with opposite spins

items.stem: What is the electron configuration of sodium (Z = 11)?
items.markingKey: C. 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s¹. Fill in order of energy

items.stem: Why is 4s filled before 3d in potassium?
items.answer: The 4s subshell is lower in energy than 3d at that point
options: The 4s subshell is lower in energy than 3d at that point
items.markingKey: B. The 4s subshell is lower in energy than 3d at that point. Aufbau principle

items.stem: Across a period from left to right, atomic radius generally
items.markingKey: D. decreases. Greater nuclear charge pulls electrons closer

items.stem: Which element has the highest first ionisation energy in Period 3?
items.markingKey: C. argon. Noble gas, full shell

items.stem: Why is the first ionisation energy of aluminium lower than that of magnesium?
items.answer: The outer electron of Al is in a 3p orbital, higher in energy and more shielded
options: Al has a full outer shell
The outer electron of Al is in a 3p orbital, higher in energy and more shielded
items.markingKey: D. The outer electron of Al is in a 3p orbital, higher in energy and more shielded. Subshell effect

items.stem: A covalent bond is
items.markingKey: A. a shared pair of electrons. Atoms share electrons

items.stem: What is the shape of a methane (CH₄) molecule?
items.markingKey: B. tetrahedral. Four bonding pairs, 109.5°

items.stem: Why is the bond angle in water (about 104.5°) smaller than in methane?
items.answer: Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs
options: Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs
items.markingKey: A. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs. VSEPR theory

items.stem: Solve x² - 7x + 12 = 0.
What is sin 30°?
items.markingKey: D. 1/2. Standard value

items.stem: If tan θ = 3/4 and θ is acute, what is sin θ?
items.markingKey: D. 3/5. A 3-4-5 triangle

items.stem: What is the 10th term of 4, 7, 10, ...?
Which term of 5, 9, 13, ... is 81?
The sum of the first n odd numbers 1 + 3 + 5 + ... is
items.markingKey: C. n². Sum of an AP

items.stem: A coin is tossed and a die is rolled. What is P(head and a 6)?
A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. What is P(both red)?
P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A and B) = 0.2. What is P(A or B)?
items.markingKey: D. 0.7. P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)

items.stem: If x² - 6x + 5 is written as (x - a)² + b, what is a?
items.markingKey: D. 3. Half of -6

items.stem: Complete the square: x² + 4x + 7 = (x + 2)² + c. What is c?
What is the minimum value of x² - 8x + 20?
If f(x) = 2x + 1, what is f(4)?
If f(x) = x + 3 and g(x) = 2x, what is f(g(5))?
What is the inverse of f(x) = 3x - 6?
items.markingKey: A. f⁻¹(x) = (x + 6)/3. Swap x and y, then solve

items.stem: How many radians are in 180°?
items.markingKey: B. π. Half a turn

items.stem: Convert 60° to radians.
What is the length of an arc of radius 6 cm subtending 2 radians at the centre?
items.markingKey: B. 12 cm. s = rθ

items.stem: How many ways can 3 different books be arranged on a shelf?
How many ways can a committee of 2 be chosen from 5 people?
What is the coefficient of x² in (1 + x)⁵?
items.markingKey: C. 10. ⁵C₂

items.stem: A cross between two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt x Tt) gives what ratio of tall to dwarf?
items.markingKey: A. 3 : 1. TT, Tt, Tt are tall; tt is dwarf

items.stem: Aerobic respiration produces
items.markingKey: B. carbon dioxide and water. Glucose + oxygen → CO₂ + water

items.stem: Why does aerobic respiration release more energy than anaerobic respiration?
items.markingKey: A. Glucose is fully broken down. Anaerobic breakdown is incomplete

items.stem: Differences between individuals of the same species are called
items.markingKey: B. variation. Genetic and environmental causes

items.stem: Which is an example of continuous variation in humans?
items.markingKey: C. height. It has a range of values

items.stem: Why does variation within a population matter for natural selection?
items.answer: Some variants survive and reproduce better, passing on their alleles
options: Some variants survive and reproduce better, passing on their alleles
items.markingKey: A. Some variants survive and reproduce better, passing on their alleles. Selection acts on variation

items.stem: An organism that eats only plants is a
items.markingKey: A. herbivore. Primary consumer

items.stem: Why do pyramids of biomass usually narrow towards the top?
items.answer: Energy and biomass are lost at each trophic level
options: Energy and biomass are lost at each trophic level
items.markingKey: A. Energy and biomass are lost at each trophic level. Respiration and waste

items.stem: A pesticide becomes more concentrated in birds of prey than in insects. This is called
items.markingKey: A. biological magnification. It builds up along the food chain

items.stem: The basic unit of life is the
items.markingKey: D. cell. Cell theory

items.stem: Which organelle is found in prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
items.markingKey: B. ribosome. Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes

items.stem: Why can electron microscopes show more detail than light microscopes?
items.answer: Electrons have a much shorter wavelength, giving higher resolution
options: Electrons have a much shorter wavelength, giving higher resolution
items.markingKey: A. Electrons have a much shorter wavelength, giving higher resolution. Resolution depends on wavelength

items.stem: Proteins are made of
items.markingKey: D. amino acids. Joined by peptide bonds

items.stem: Which test identifies a reducing sugar?
items.markingKey: A. Benedict's test. Brick-red precipitate

items.stem: Why does a change in one amino acid sometimes stop a protein working?
items.answer: It can change the folding and so the shape of the active part
options: It can change the folding and so the shape of the active part
items.markingKey: B. It can change the folding and so the shape of the active part. Shape determines function

items.stem: Enzymes are biological
items.markingKey: B. catalysts. They speed up reactions

items.stem: Why does an enzyme stop working at high temperature?
items.answer: Its active site changes shape (it is denatured)
options: Its active site changes shape (it is denatured)
items.markingKey: D. Its active site changes shape (it is denatured). Bonds holding its shape break

items.stem: A competitive inhibitor slows an enzyme by
items.answer: binding to the active site and blocking the substrate
options: binding to the active site and blocking the substrate
items.markingKey: A. binding to the active site and blocking the substrate. It resembles the substrate

items.stem: Movement of molecules against a concentration gradient using energy is
items.markingKey: C. active transport. ATP is needed

items.stem: Mitosis produces
items.markingKey: A. two genetically identical daughter cells. For growth and repair

items.stem: Why is cancer described as a disease of the cell cycle?
items.answer: Cells divide by mitosis in an uncontrolled way
options: Cells divide by mitosis in an uncontrolled way
items.markingKey: B. Cells divide by mitosis in an uncontrolled way. Control of the cycle fails

items.stem: What number comes next? 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ?
items.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two before it

items.stem: Money doubles in 6 years at a fixed compound rate. In how many years does it become 8 times?
Boys and girls in a class are in the ratio 3 : 5. After 6 more boys join, the ratio is 1 : 1. How many students were there at first?
One pipe fills a tank in 6 hours; another empties it in 9 hours. If both are open, how long does it take to fill the empty tank?
Which phrase is closest in meaning to 'ubiquitous'?
Author is to novel as composer is to ...
Some economists are writers. All writers are readers. Which statement must be true?
items.explanation: The economists who are writers are also readers

items.stem: Claim: 'Since the new study app launched, the school's test scores rose, so the app raised scores.' Which fact, if true, most weakens the claim?
options: The school also hired extra teachers at the same time
Students said they liked the app
items.answer: The school also hired extra teachers at the same time
items.explanation: Another change at the same time offers a different explanation

items.stem: What comes next? AZ, BY, CX, ?
items.explanation: First letters go forward, second letters go backward

items.stem: What comes next? 1, 2, 6, 24, 120, ?
Figures: shaded triangle, unshaded square, shaded pentagon, ... Each figure gains one side and the shading alternates. What is the next figure?
items.explanation: Six sides, and the shading switches back to unshaded

items.stem: What is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 3:15?
items.explanation: The hour hand has moved a quarter of 30° past the 3

items.stem: From home you walk 4 km north and then 3 km east. How far are you from home in a straight line?
A 3 x 3 x 3 cube is painted on all faces and cut into 27 small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly one painted face?
items.explanation: One at the centre of each face
